title: Stanford men's golf opens spring season with match play against Texas A&M - South SFV Today
text:
Stanford University’s men’s golf team will begin its 2026 season with a match-play event against Texas A&M on Sunday, January 25, at The Vintage Club in Indian Wells, California. This marks the Cardinal’s return to competition after a three-month break.
The Vintage Club offers two courses for the event: the Mountain Course, which is a par-72 layout stretching 7,138 yards and features Fazio-style bunkering and bent grass greens; and the Desert Course, a 6,515-yard par-72 track recognized by the American Society of Golf Course Architects as one of the top three courses built in the last two decades.
The matchup is between two teams ranked in the Top 40 nationally. Stanford enters ranked No. 35 while Texas A&M holds the No. 31 spot. Texas A&M’s lineup includes Aaron Pounds (No. 29) and Wheaton Ennis (No. 89), both inside the top-100 individual rankings. Stanford counters with TK Chantananuwat (No. 90) and Jay Leng (No. 109).
The tournament will use an 18-hole match play format with eight points available for contention.
Live scoring will be provided via Scoreboard by Clippd, and updates can be followed on X and Instagram at @StanfordMGolf.
Stanford’s lineup for this weekend features all eight team members, including junior Kush Arora making his season debut. Returning players Nathan Wang, Jay Leng, Edan Cui, Dean Greyserman, Ethan Gao, and Cooper Stearns last competed at the Golf Club of Georgia Collegiate before winter break. TK Chantananuwat rejoins after finishing tied for 11th at the Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship.
Last season, Stanford narrowly lost to Texas A&M in their previous meeting at the Hideaway Shootout by a score of 5-4. Victories for Stanford came from Dean Greyserman (-3), Sean-Karl Dobson (even), Logan Kim (-1), and TK Chantananuwat (-1).
Dean Greyserman recently became the third consecutive Stanford player to win the Silicon Valley Amateur title as Stanford hosted the event at home. He led throughout all three rounds and finished at 12-under par; teammate Edan Cui was runner-up at 10-under.
Freshman Edan Cui achieved his best collegiate result at the Golf Club of Georgia Collegiate by tying for sixth place after leading through two rounds.
At last fall’s Hamptons Intercollegiate tournament, both Dean Greyserman and Jay Leng earned their first career top-10 finishes for Stanford.
TK Chantananuwat recorded his third career top-10 finish during October’s Ben Hogan Collegiate Invitational presented by Charles Schwab.
Stanford retained its Big Match title against California in a playoff decided by Megha Ganne’s long putt alongside Dean Greyserman.
In September’s OFCC/Fighting Illini Invitational that opened this season, TK Chantananuwat led Stanford with a tie for 24th place as several other teammates finished within or near the top-50.
Nathan Wang was named to last year’s All-ACC Team following four top-20 finishes and posting a team-best scoring average over thirty rounds.
First-year players TK Chantananuwat and Jay Leng each played every event last season for Stanford and notched multiple top-20 finishes apiece.
Senior Dean Greyserman had notable summer success on the east coast by winning two tournaments—including an automatic berth into this year’s U.S. Amateur Championship—and competing in several MGA events.
Stanford added two new recruits this year: Edan Cui—ranked No. 41 nationally among juniors—and Cooper Stearns—the Orange County Boys Athlete of the Year who also played basketball at Irvine High School.
